headline: Margin expansion drives earnings growth, guidance raised

kpis.label: Component Repair Services Adj. EBITDA margin %

summary_short: StandardAero grew Q2 2026 revenue 4.6% y/y to $1,599.7M and net income 43.7% to $97.3M ($0.29 diluted GAAP EPS), as Adjusted EBITDA rose 12.3% to $229.9M on a record 14.4% margin, prompting a raise to full-year revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, and Adjusted Diluted EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue rose 4.6% y/y on commercial aerospace and business aviation demand, partly offset by the planned elimination of low-margin pass-through revenue and lower military sales. Net income grew 43.7% to $97.3M ($0.29 diluted GAAP EPS; $0.40 Adjusted Diluted EPS, +24% y/y) as Adjusted EBITDA rose 12.3% to $229.9M and margin hit a record 14.4%, aided by productivity gains and the pass-through elimination; Engine Services turned profitable on LEAP and CFM56 DFW. Component Repair Services margin fell 270bps to 26.3% on unfavorable mix. Free cash flow was a $50.2M inflow versus a $30.7M outflow a year ago. Cash was $179.1M, debt $2,301.8M, net debt/Adjusted EBITDA improved to 2.6x from 3.0x. StandardAero raised FY2026 revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, and Adjusted Diluted EPS guidance.

ADJUSTED DILUTED EPS DEFINITION CHANGE: effective this quarter, the company broadened its Adjusted Diluted EPS exclusion from acquisition-related intangible amortization to ALL intangible amortization (including license-related intangibles), and correspondingly redefined guidance for 'Adjusted Free Cash Flow' to exclude all intangible-asset purchases rather than only acquisition-related ones -- both prior-period and forward figures in this summary use the new, broader definition as stated by the company; comparisons to $0.32 (Q2 2025 Adjusted Diluted EPS) are as restated/recast by the release itself, not independently recomputed. GAAP EPS BASIS: Basic EPS was $0.30 (vs $0.21 y/y); this summary reports Diluted GAAP EPS ($0.29 vs $0.20 y/y) as the primary GAAP figure per the release's own headline framing. TOTAL CASH SWING: the y/y and (SEC-verbatim shard) q/q comparisons for total cash reflect a large intra-year swing -- cash fell from $289.7M (Dec 31, 2025) to an implied Q1 2026 trough near $89.2M on a working-capital-heavy first quarter (H1 operating cash flow was -$47.2M despite Q2 alone being +$72.3M), before partially recovering to $179.1M at Q2-end on debt draws and improved Q2 operating performance; no cross-basis or absurd-surprise issues found. All figures reconcile to the primary press release, Exhibit 99.1.

drivers.explanation: CEO Russell Ford cited robust demand across served commercial aerospace platforms, elimination of pass-through revenue, and supply-chain initiatives as behind the EBITDA growth, record margins, and free-cash-flow inflow, supporting the guidance raise.

Driven by continued demand growth in commercial aerospace (+5.7% y/y) and business aviation (+5.6% y/y), partly offset by elimination of low-to-no margin pass-through revenue and lower military sales.
Increase primarily due to productivity improvements and the elimination of material pass-through revenue on restructured contracts.
Follows the 24.3% rise in operating income and a $2.6M y/y decline in interest expense, partly offset by higher income tax expense.
Growth reflects the underlying earnings increase plus a broadened, company-disclosed intangible-amortization addback effective this quarter that now also excludes license-related intangibles.
Growth across all three major end markets, offset by the elimination of low-to-no margin material pass-through revenues on restructured contracts.
Driven by productivity gains, elimination of pass-through revenue, and favorable mix, partly offset by the continued ramp of the LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs.
Strong demand on commercial aerospace products and aeroderivative platforms, partly offset by lower military-platform revenue due to input delays.
